newsitem.title: USA: Ex Atlanta Fed chief Forrestal sees no FOMC move.
newsitem.headline: Ex Atlanta Fed chief Forrestal sees no FOMC move.

text.p: Former Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank chief Robert Forrestal said he expects policy makers to leave U.S. monetary policy unchanged at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on February 4 and 5.

"We've seen a lot of labor shortages but so far that has not been translated into very substantial wage increases. So I think it's premature to think the Fed is going to move on the basis of wage information that it has at the moment," Forrestal said in an interview with CNBC cable network.
"I think they are going to be watching it carefully but they're going to take a wait-and-see attitude," he added.
Forrestal also said the inflation scenario remained positive, which could leave the Federal Reserve in a waiting pattern for some time in the future.

"I think with the slowing economy, which I think will happen, and inflation fairly quiet at the moment, I think the Fed is going to be in a waiting pattern, a wait-and-see pattern for some months to come," Forrestal said.
